title: stackunderflow.anchor/1 agent-continuity envelope
description: The stable, versioned contract for `stax-rs anchor get --json` and `stax-rs anchor log --json`. Anchors are a keyed, append-only, timestamped state store an agent writes at every decision (`anchor set`) and re-reads after a context rotation (`anchor get --json` at session start) -- the ARCHITECT-STATE.md continuity pattern, productized. ORIGIN: added by the Rust-port campaign (rust/TASKS-RS.md RS-1-029..033); the Rust CLI is the first producer, and the envelope is renderered by stax-core's `anchor::render_json`. WIRE RULES: (1) key order is part of the contract -- producers emit the keys in the order this schema lists them (serde_json `preserve_order`, the wave-0 workspace decision), so goldens are compared byte for byte; (2) rendering is pretty-printed with a two-space indent and exactly one trailing newline, matching contracts/stackunderflow-memory-v1; (3) non-ASCII is emitted VERBATIM UTF-8 -- unlike stackunderflow.memory/1, which is produced by Python's `json.dumps` default and therefore \u-escapes. A Python producer of this contract must pass ensure_ascii=False. (4) There is no error envelope: a failure goes to stderr with a non-zero exit and stdout stays empty, so stdout is either a complete envelope or nothing. An empty result -- unknown key, or no sidecar in this directory -- is a SUCCESS with `anchors: []`. Objects are intentionally open (no additionalProperties:false) so an unknown ADDITIVE field stays forward-compatible.

db.description: Absolute path of the sidecar that answered. Present because the default sidecar is cwd-local (./.stax-anchors.db, project-scoped like .git): when `anchors` comes back empty, this field is the difference between 'nothing was ever anchored' and 'you are in the wrong directory'. Resolution order: --db flag, then $STAX_ANCHOR_DB, then <cwd>/.stax-anchors.db.

generated.description: When this envelope was rendered. RFC 3339 UTC, millisecond precision, literal Z -- the same shape store.db uses for first_ts/last_ts.

anchors.description: For `get`: the newest entry of each key, ordered by key under SQLite's BINARY collation (byte order, locale-independent). For `log`: one key's entire history, oldest first. NEWEST means LAST APPENDED, not largest `ts`: storage is append-only and ordered by insertion, so a clock that jumps backwards cannot reorder history. Bodies are carried VERBATIM and are never truncated -- an anchor is meant to be spliced into a context window as-is, so the token bound comes from the caller keeping bodies anchor-sized and from `get` returning one entry per key.

anchor_count.description: len(anchors). Redundant by construction and checked by the fixture runner; present so a consumer can branch without materialising the array.

schema_tag.description: The frozen contract id. The trailing integer is the MAJOR version and bumps only on a breaking change to the envelope; a consumer pins it and refuses an unknown major.

command.description: Which read produced this envelope. Both shapes carry `anchors[]`, and this is what says whether the array is newest-per-key (`get`) or one key's history (`log`). ADDITIVE enum: a new producer appends a value without bumping the major.

query.description: Echo of the resolved input, so a caller can correlate a response with the call that produced it.

key.description: The key that was asked for; null for a bare `anchor get`, which returns every key's newest entry.

anchor.description: One appended anchor. Immutable: entries are only ever INSERTed (SQLite triggers refuse UPDATE and DELETE), so a `log` is an audit trail rather than a mutable document.

key.description: The caller's key -- architect-state, wave-state, ... Free-form and never blank; stable keys are the point, since `get` returns one row per key.

ts.description: When the anchor was appended. RFC 3339 UTC, millisecond precision, literal Z. Two anchors written inside the same millisecond share a `ts` and are still ordered by insertion.

session_hint.description: Best-effort id of the session that wrote the anchor, read from $CLAUDE_SESSION_ID at write time; null when the variable was unset or blank. Nothing keys off it -- it is a breadcrumb back to indexed session history, which is what a store-less notes tool cannot offer.

body.description: The anchored text, byte-verbatim as supplied (positional TEXT, --file, or stdin). Trailing newlines from a file or a pipe are preserved. A body that is only whitespace is refused at write time, so this is never blank.
